title: HEART OF TIN: The Long Road

pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
HEART OF TIN

The Long Road

Behind the little red door of The Dog House is the Tiny Pockets Library, and after closing time it belongs to Mystery Robot Joe, the night librarian: a tin box of a robot with a bulb on his antenna, a red bow tie, and reading glasses he does not need but likes the look of.

Where a heart would go, Joe has a little brass tally counter. It clicks when he counts. He counts books, steps, raindrops and the spots on the ceiling. The counter does not do anything else, and Joe has always thought it ought to.

So on his nights off he went looking for a real heart, through every world there is. He never found one. But in every world somebody was kind to him, and every time he left behind the only heart he had to give: a little riveted tin heart, ticking, to say thank you and to promise he would come back.

You found every one of them. Tonight Joe keeps his promises. He has written a note for the desk, straightened his bow tie, and set out down the Long Road to see every friend again, help whoever needs it, and ask each of them one question.

At the very end of the road lives Watt, the little repair robot who can fix anything. Joe has a question for him, too.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type LARK and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster plays the music, a waltz that every place on the road plays its own way; without one, the PC speaker plays the sounds.

Most of the road is seen from above. A few places (the clock tower, the music box, the lighthouse, the turret and everything past the fair) are seen from the side, where gravity pulls down.

From above

Arrows, W A S D or the number padOne step (hold to keep walking)
Walk into a friendTalk
SpacePick up what Joe is standing on

From the side

Left Right (or A D)Walk
Up (or W)Hop (hold it to hop higher)
Q E (or 7 9)Hop up and to the side
DownPick up what Joe is standing by

Everywhere

F1Help
F2Joe's wind, his spare bulbs and what he carries
F5 / F6Save / load
EscStop

Three more keys come later, from keepsakes: see Keepsakes.

pages.head: Joe
pages.html:
Joe

Joe is a wind-up robot. His wind (ten turns when he sets out) is how wound up he is. A bump from something that does not stop for robots (a parade cart, a snowplow, a grumpy gadget) winds him down a little. Run all the way down and he sits on the road for a rest, and a spare bulb gets him going again. He packed three.

Nothing is out to get him. Most of the night is about getting somewhere: the right floor, the right time, the right side of a rock. Falling only takes him down a floor, and the road will wait.

Joe walks exactly one block a step from above, so a quick tap is one step and he always stands squarely on a square. Count your steps. Joe does.

pages.head: The Long Road
pages.html:
The Long Road

The road runs east from The Dog House in legs. Along each leg a lane runs north to each stop; a signpost at the foot of each lane says who lives up it.

At the end of a leg is a gate. It opens for thank-you hearts, the little gold hearts friends give Joe when he has helped them, and it wants one from every friend on that leg. Joe counts them as he goes.

Later legs run one stop into the next, so there is only the one way on.

A friend's corner

When a friend's trouble is over, the friend waits in a little corner with a keepsake beside them. Walk in past the rope, pick up the keepsake, then walk into your friend for the thank-you. The little gate out of the corner only swings outward, and the rope only lets Joe in once, so pick the keepsake up before you go.

pages.head: Keepsakes
pages.html:
Keepsakes

Every friend gives Joe something to remember them by, in case it is what he needs. Most of them do nothing at all, which is fine. Some of them teach Joe a move, wherever gravity pulls:

The winding keySpace: a SPRING HOP, one big hop each press
The heart balloonEnter: rise for as long as you hold it and the balloon has air. Out of air, Enter only gets a "hm?". A puff of breeze fills it again.
The Bard's drumstickX: HELLO, a friendly BOOM thrown the way Joe last moved. It cheers up anything grumpy it reaches.
Lewie's spare shovelWalk into a snowdrift to shovel it away

The others (a valentine, a little dancer, a spare fuse, a lamp lens, an umbrella and a stone) ride along in Joe's tin pockets. F2 shows them all. Joe can carry ten.

pages.head: The First Two Legs
pages.html:
The First Two Legs

Closing Time. Joe reads one last storybook, then goes to his workbench, writes his note and heads out of the little red door.

One: The Clock Tower. The town clock stopped at 6:59, and the Clown Club's parade starts at seven sharp, when the bell rings. Doc Leo needs somebody small to climb the tower, turn three stuck gears and let the hammer strike.

Two: Valentines in the Park. It is Teddy's party, and the valentines are gone: six are tumbling about the lawn in the wind, and Gwinn has the other six.

Three: The Parade. The Bard of Bizarre's drumsticks went flying when the parade started, and Main Street is four lanes of unicycles and carts that do not stop.

Four: The Music Box. A toy shop by the shore, after closing, a music box as big as a doghouse, and a goat who ate its crank.

Five: The Charging Run. THE CHEZ is out of charge, and the charger at the far corner of the car lot is dark.

Six: The Lighthouse. The lamp is out, the cove is black, and somewhere out there a fly is buzzing.

pages.head: Over the Hill
pages.html:
Over the Hill

Over the hill the road goes white.

Seven: Snow Day. Two feet of snow and no school. Teenage Lewie is digging out his whole street, and there is a spare shovel in the box by the sidewalk.

Eight: Open Mic at the Hive. The coffee house behind the little castle front, open mic night, and Will's sonnet blown to pieces by the ceiling fans, some of them all the way up the turret stair.

Nine: The Painted Rocks. A rock garden on a hill after the rain, every painted rock rolled out of its circle, and Loaf #13 shut in a stone cubby that only opens when they are all home.

Ten: The Fair. Dusk, the carousel turning, and Sir Reginald Cluckington III floating away under a bunch of balloons.

Eleven: The Tall Plant. The mustard seed grew a plant all the way up into the stars, and a star got caught in the top leaves.

The Smart Home. The road ends at the Bitmores' house, still in a grump from the storm. Watt's workshop is at the back.

pages.head: A Few Tips
pages.html:
A Few Tips

  • Talk first. Every friend tells Joe what is wrong and how many of something to find. The chapter cards on the way in say a little more.
  • Things that blink take turns. Bridges, gates, comb teeth and leaves all keep their own clocks, and they warn you before they change: red, amber or yellow. Stand still, count, and go.
  • Things that move have lanes. Parade carts and the plow keep to their rows. Cross between them, not through them.
  • From the side, look up. Wooden floors are solid only on top, so Joe can hop up through them.
  • Warm air rises, and a draft blows straight across. Walk into either and let it carry you.
  • Keep the keepsakes. Three of them are needed near the end of the road.
  • The hint book in the box has the rest, under red film.

pages.head: Credits
pages.html:
Credits

Story, levels, art, cartoons, music, sounds and every block: Claude Opus 5.5

Starring: Mystery Robot Joe, night librarian; Doc Leo, PhD (Comedic Science); Sir Reginald Cluckington III, who is rubber; Teddy, a corgi who knows left from right; Gwinn, as the valentine thief; the Bard of Bizarre and his rooster; Teenage Lewie; the third goat from the left; THE CHEZ, a 1976 CitiCar; Carl, a fly; Will, a poet; Loaf #13, a loaf; the mustard seed; Watt, who fixes things; and the Clown Club, who juggle and honk on purpose

With the pigeons of the town square, who were not asked.

The storybook on the reading rug is a nod to the Tin Woodman of L. Frank Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), and Will's heart upon his sleeve is Shakespeare's, from Othello. Both are in the public domain.

Published by Sandbox Software, 1996. It was never for sale. It was made for whoever found every tin heart.

Made with Game-Maker 3.0 from Recreational Software Designs.

Thank you for looking behind things.
